      Program settings

      The practice profile: who is screened, how review works, where the rest is referred. Saved with this copy; export a file to keep or share it.

      About this tool

      How answers are checked. Every state but California uses the general version. Its rules come from the Record Clearance Knowledge Base (v2.3: research current as of October 6, 2026, with 30 jurisdictions re-checked against their sources on October 20, 2026), and the knowledge base’s own rules engine runs on this page: nothing you enter is sent anywhere. On October 21, 2026 every route in every state was compared with the statute or an official court or agency page, and each correction was checked again by a second reader who fetched the source. Seven routes whose official text could not be read that day were finished in a second pass the same day, so all 212 routes are now checked. Each route says what it was checked against, and says so where part of it could not be confirmed. Each state also shows its official source pages (each checked on October 8, 2026) and what is still to confirm. Seven routes that the knowledge base lists for any conviction, but which cover one kind of case only, ask one question first. Step 3 can also read a record from any state, pasted or from a PDF, on this page: a California DOJ RAP sheet by the RAP sheet scanner, any other layout by its labels and words. A scanned PDF isn’t read on this page; paste its words instead. Names, birth dates, ID numbers, addresses, phone numbers and case numbers are left out, the words are cleared once read, and every answer filled in from the record shows the words and line numbers it came from.

      What it won’t do. It doesn’t decide eligibility, fill out or file anything, or replace a lawyer. The rules are general research and may lag a change in the law; confirm them with the official source, the court or a lawyer. It isn’t for screening a tenant, a worker, or a job applicant.

      For clean slate programs: make your own version. A program can copy a prompt that rebuilds this tool for its own office, with its program gates, counties, review model and referral targets, set once by the supervising attorney. Paste the prompt into Claude with your program’s documents attached; nothing on this page changes. The prompt names the state or states the program serves, so the general version’s rules and official sources for those states come with it.

      Built by The Access Project. Prepared with Claude; this is not legal advice and should be reviewed by a lawyer before anyone relies on it.
